🙏 High on a hill on the western edge of Kathmandu, the eyes of the Buddha look out over the whole valley.

This is Swayambhunath. Pilgrims climb to the great white stupa at first light, walk around it clockwise, spin the prayer wheels and light butter lamps among the small stone shrines. Hindus and Buddhists both come here to pray.

And yes — the monkeys who live on the hill are part of the morning. Keep snacks out of sight 🐒

🛕 Our 3-day Kathmandu Heritage & Culture tour begins here on Day 1, with Kathmandu Durbar Square — private to your family, with a guide who knows the stories behind every shrine.

Our 7-day Bhutan journey: land in the Paro valley, two unhurried days in the capital Thimphu, over the prayer-flag-draped Dochula Pass to the riverside dzong at Punakha — then the hike to Taktsang, the Tiger's Nest, clinging to a cliff some 900 metres above the valley floor. A licensed Bhutanese guide and private driver throughout, visa arranged by us, private to your group.

Walk into a glacial amphitheatre ringed by giants — Annapurna I (8,091 m) on one side, Machhapuchhre (6,993 m) right overhead. 🏔️

This is the Annapurna Sanctuary, and our 14-day Annapurna Base Camp Trek takes you all the way in:

🌄 Day 5 — sunrise from Poon Hill (3,210 m)
🏡 Day 6 — the Gurung village of Chhomrong
⛰️ Day 9 — Machhapuchhre Base Camp, then Annapurna Base Camp at 4,130 m
♨️ Day 11 — down to Jhinu Danda

Lower than Everest Base Camp, well-marked, and achievable for motivated beginners with good fitness. Private to your group, with a licensed guide, porters, ACAP permit and TIMS card included.

Turquoise glacial lakes above 4,700 metres, and four of the world's 8,000-metre peaks in one sunrise. 💎🏔️

The Gokyo Lakes Trek takes the Khumbu's quieter western valleys: Namche, Dole, Machhermo, then the glacial lakes of Gokyo. At dawn, climb Gokyo Ri (5,357 m) for Everest, Lhotse, Makalu and Cho Oyu at once, with the vast Ngozumpa Glacier below. Our 17-day route then crosses Cho La. Private to your group, with acclimatisation built in.

Flying from India to Nepal? Check this before you leave for the airport. ✈️

The Embassy of India in Kathmandu lists only two documents as valid for Indian nationals travelling by air between India and Nepal:

🛂 A valid Indian passport
🪪 OR your original Voter ID card with photograph, issued by the Election Commission of India

❌ Aadhaar, PAN card and driving licence are not accepted
❌ A downloaded or printed-online Voter ID is not accepted either — carry the original

No visa is needed for Indian nationals. Rules can change, so always check the embassy's page before you fly — the link is in the first comment.
